title: Columbus, 1492 — the sailor who saw land first, and the reward he never got
sources: Wikipedia: Voyages of Christopher Columbus — sailed west in search of a route to India, China, Japan and the Spice Islands; three ships, the carrack Santa María and the caravels Pinta and Niña; on 10 October Columbus quelled a mutiny by sailors who wanted to abandon the search and return to Spain; at around 10 PM on 11 October Columbus thought he saw a light 'like a little wax candle rising and falling'; four hours later land was sighted by a sailor named Rodrigo de Triana; Columbus called the island San Salvador, its Indigenous name was Guanahani; he insisted he had reached Asia; Columbus died in 1506, and the next year the New World was named 'America' after Amerigo Vespucci; Columbus later participated in the beginning of the Spanish conquest of the Americas

Wikipedia: Christopher Columbus — left Palos on 3 August 1492; a five-week voyage across the ocean from La Gomera; on 7 October 'immense flocks of birds'; at around 02:00 a lookout on the Pinta, Rodrigo de Triana, spotted land; Columbus later maintained he had already seen a light hours earlier, thereby claiming for himself the lifetime pension promised by Ferdinand and Isabella to the first person to sight land; he called the inhabitants Los Indios; over his later voyages he refused to acknowledge that the lands were not part of Asia
Wikipedia: Rodrigo de Triana — on the Pinta, sighted land at about two in the morning on 12 October 1492; is reported to have shouted '¡Tierra! ¡Tierra!'

Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1799 Jeanne Geneviève Garnerin becomes the first woman to make a parachute descent; 1960 Nikita Khrushchev pounds his shoe on a desk at the United Nations

Prang & Co., 1893); Waldseemüller map, 1507
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): a galleon replica under sail, a ship at sunset, gulls over the sea, moonlight on the sea, a candle, a tropical beach

post.facebook:
On this day in 1492, Christopher Columbus's ships reached an island in the Bahamas: Guanahani to its people, San Salvador to Columbus.

The voyage had nearly ended two days earlier, when sailors who wanted to turn back rose against him. Then came "immense flocks of birds", and debris floating on the sea.

King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella had promised a lifetime pension to the first person to sight land. At about two in the morning, a lookout on the Pinta, Rodrigo de Triana, did — and is said to have shouted "¡Tierra! ¡Tierra!" But Columbus maintained that four hours earlier he had seen a light "like a little wax candle rising and falling". The pension went to Columbus.

He was sure he had reached Asia, and called the people he met "Indians". For them, it was the beginning of the Spanish conquest. Columbus never accepted that the lands were not Asia — and the year after he died in 1506, the New World was named after another explorer: Amerigo Vespucci.

Also on 12 October: Jeanne Geneviève Garnerin became the first woman to make a parachute jump (1799), and Khrushchev pounded his shoe at the UN (1960).

youtube.description:
12 October 1492: after five weeks at sea and a near-mutiny, a lookout on the Pinta, Rodrigo de Triana, spotted land at two in the morning. The king and queen had promised a lifetime pension to the first to see land — but Columbus said he had seen a light hours earlier, "like a little wax candle", and took the reward himself. He was sure he had reached Asia. The year after he died, the New World was named after another man: Amerigo Vespucci.

Also on 12 October: the first woman's parachute jump (1799) and Khrushchev's shoe at the UN (1960).
